The coefficients 1−(i−j)/(k−j) express total mass on any balanced row. Their strict signs force all entries except the terminal one; that entry is then fixed by balance. This proves global optimality and uniqueness without a regularity assumption.

The same allocation is shared by all maximal-mass sources. Integrating the top and bottom fills gives opposite spread terms of size m_i*(w_i−m_i)/2 and average m_i*(l_i+u_i)/2. Thus the displayed value is the path midpoint.

The retained bases are consecutive. Full retained fibers lie in the new hull and cannot grow because it is contained in C. A proper partial interval is extreme and cannot grow by combinations with other bases. This realizes exactly the chosen lengths and centroid.

The inherited length measure of the hull is dominated by the original measure on every ambient closed cap. The accepted strict one-third bound applies when the hull has at least two positive fibers; otherwise direct interval bisection gives T_j/2. T_j≥3M/4 therefore suffices in either case.
